reason: The bent antenna seems the most direct obstacle to hearing Earth's message, and the service tool may straighten it.
expectation: I expect to repair or free the antenna for mounting, though it may need another part.

alternatives.reason: Insulating the window also addresses a goal, but I want to start with the radio.

effect: The antenna is straightened, so I can try installing it on the mount.
reaction: This matched my expectation; it is a straightforward repair.
reason: Mounting the antenna seems the next practical step toward a working radio.
expectation: I expect the antenna to be installed, perhaps restoring reception or revealing another requirement.

effect: The radio works and the twelve-minute-old message establishes that a reply will take time; I can turn to the cabin.
reaction: The delayed voice is a compelling, concrete reminder of distance.
reason: Foil and felt seem like materials for insulating the heat-losing window.
expectation: I expect a layered insulating cover that may need fitting to the window.

alternatives.reason: Charging the emergency battery may also prepare for night, but I want to address the stated heat loss first.

effect: The materials formed reflective quilt stock, which is offered at the window.
reaction: The result is plausible, though I am curious how it will be secured.
reason: Putting the quilt at the window should address the heat loss directly.
expectation: I expect the insulation to be fitted or prepared for fitting, possibly using the spare rail.

effect: The stock is now a window quilt and the rail can be combined with it, suggesting it still needs mounting.
reaction: The rail offers a satisfying practical next step, although the distinction between stock and quilt is terse.
reason: The rail should hold the quilt over the window.
expectation: I expect a mounted or operable insulating curtain and progress on keeping the cabin ready.

effect: The quilt now slides and reduces the felt cold, but the night goal remains open.
reaction: The cold easing and morning view make the repair feel tangible and lived in.
reason: Charging the battery is the only available combination and seems useful for night backup.
expectation: I expect the battery to charge from the array and contribute to the remaining goal.

effect: Charging the reserve completes the night preparation, and the fuel-cell backup explains how essential systems can endure darkness.
reaction: The connection to the recovered array is satisfying, although the battery and fuel-cell relationship is a little unclear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Mounting the antenna brought a twelve-minute-old voice into the cabin; that made the distance to Earth feel immediate and gave the repair a human purpose.

leastWorthwhile.text: Turning reflective stock into a window quilt was terse, so I could not tell what physical work occurred at that step.

surprise.text: The voice was already twelve minutes old and the reply would come later; that made the communication delay concrete.

arbitrary.text: The window stock becoming a quilt at the window felt somewhat unexplained, although its insulation purpose was clear. The other combinations had understandable purposes.

continue.text: Yes. The delayed message and the sensory detail of the sliding quilt made me curious about daily life and what comes back from Earth, though the combinations so far were fairly direct.
